reasoning_summary: Setup checks pass. Re = 0.15*0.01/1.5e-5 = 100 matches the specification. The force references (magUInf 0.15, lRef 0.01, Aref 0.0001) are consistent. Blockage is 0.0125, with 30D upstream, 50D downstream and 40D half-height, so the unbounded treatment is reasonable. Mass imbalance is 2.5e-10.

Statistical checks pass. The record has 12 stationary cycles, and the transient ends at 73.298 against a declared averaging start of 75.0. Mean-drag CI95 is 5.2336e-05, drift is 0.00016636 and half-window difference is 7.1618e-05. The time-domain St (0.15848) matches the FFT St (0.15849). Sampling error is therefore negligible, and the averaging window is not the problem.

Discretisation error cannot be bounded, and it is the main risk against a 3 % tolerance. The evidence has one mesh (30580 cells) and one time step (0.04 convective units). There is no refinement or time-step study. The 'representative_cell_size_D' of 0.45745 is only a domain-average size. The wake mesh ends at 1.0209 D cells (111 streamwise cells), so the wake is coarse. The scheme is first-order Euler in time with max Courant 2.9248 and 2 outer correctors. Numerical dissipation of that kind would damp shedding and bias both mean drag (1.2901) and St (0.15849).

Both reported quantities sit slightly low in the same direction, which fits an under-resolved, dissipative wake. This is only a suspicion, not proof. Nothing in the evidence shows grid or time-step independence, and the St frequency resolution of 0.013333 is itself about 8 % of St. I therefore do not trust either quantity to 3 %. Confidence is low because no hard defect is recorded.
